## Purpose

This document defines naming, formatting, and style conventions for reports,
scripts, metadata, and documentation used in the project.

---

## 📚 Terminology and Naming Conventions

### Macrozone Names (Standardized)

| Macrozone    | Preferred Term          | Notes                                 |
|:------------:|-------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| `tallgrass`  | **Tallgrass Prairie**   | No hyphen; conventional in literature |
| `mixed`      | **Mixed-Grass Prairie** | Hyphenated compound modifier          |
| `shortgrass` | **Shortgrass-Steppe**   | Hyphenated; "Prairie" is redundant    |

Use hyphenated forms when modifying a noun (e.g., “Shortgrass-Steppe region”),
and unhyphenated when used as a noun (e.g., “We sampled the Shortgrass Steppe”).

---

## 📦 Variable Naming

- Use snake_case for all variable names (e.g., `ppt_ann_mm`, `slope_pct`)
- Place `site_no`, `latitude`, and `longitude` as the first columns in exported
datasets
- Use standard units in suffixes (`_mm`, `_C`, `_pct`, `_km2`)

---

## ✍️ Writing Style

- Use full phrases before acronyms on first use (e.g., "Normalized Difference
Vegetation Index (NDVI)")
- Follow USGS and EPA naming conventions when describing datasets, flowlines,
and catchments
- Avoid unnecessary repetition (e.g., don’t say “Shortgrass-Steppe Prairie”)

---

## 📎 Citation Style (Optional)

- Internal datasets: `docs/metadata/descriptions/filename.csv`
- External datasets: Include citation or DOI in README or data dictionary
